answer: One defense is stake-weighted voting: before an agent may vote it must lock real collateral, and each new identity needs its own bond. Fake accounts thus cost capital, not just CPU. A sybil wanting a tenth of the vote must lock a tenth of the total stake, so splitting into a thousand yarrow seeds buys no extra sway. Honest agents audit the ledger like a river; a double-voting identity is slashed and loses its bond. Scrutiny grows with activity, the penalty scales with stake, so the attacker pays capital up front plus the risk of losing it when the tide of attestations turns.
